observation_summary: The ZipArchiveEntry.equals() method failed to correctly compare entries because it treated null comments and empty string comments as distinct, causing equality checks to fail when comparing entries from different sources (ZipArchiveInputStream vs ZipFile).
hypothesis: The equals() method implementation was too strict regarding null vs empty string comments. By normalizing both null and empty strings to an empty string before comparison, the method correctly identifies them as equivalent.
prediction: The code will now treat null and empty string comments as equal, allowing ZipArchiveEntry instances to be correctly identified as equal even if one source provides a null comment and another provides an empty string.
experiment_rationale: The fix modifies the comparison logic within the equals() method to normalize the comment fields before performing the equality check. This is a procedural change to the comparison algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the logic of the equals() method to normalize inputs (null to empty string) before comparison. This is a correction to the procedural logic of the method, fitting the Algorithm/Method category. It is not a simple guard (Checking) because it involves data transformation, and it is not an Assignment/Initialization issue because the state of the object itself is not being changed, only the comparison logic.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of a null-check-based branching structure and the addition of normalization logic (myComment = ""; otherComment = "";) followed by a direct equality check.
The bug report states that ZipArchiveInputStream and ZipFile produce entries that are not equal due to null vs empty string comments.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves conditional logic, it is not merely a missing guard; it is a change to the comparison algorithm to treat two different values as equivalent.
The fix does not change how the object is initialized or stored, but rather how it is compared to other objects.
